scope: Policy-independent storage and public catalog reads; preparatory FB03 slice, no privileged writes or source UI integration
architecture: Catalog owns Merchant, Outlet, Category and Item records; no cross-module identity database queries
Separate NestJS CatalogModule exporting service; resolver validates inputs; module owns its bounded PostgreSQL pool and lifecycle
Lead integrates module and SDL in app.ts, generated contracts, root docs/status
storage: UUID primary keys; publication booleans default false on merchant/outlet/category/item
Outlet belongs to merchant; category belongs to outlet; item references category using composite categoryId+outletId foreign key to prevent cross-outlet association
Bounded trimmed nonempty names max100; descriptions max2000; integer priceMinor 0..2147483647; outlet currency uppercase 3 ASCII letters, syntactic only, no market support claim
Restrict parent deletion; indexes support outlet/id keyset paging and publication filters
visibility: Return outlet only if outlet and parent merchant published
Return item only if merchant/outlet/category/item all published; available may be false and accurately serialized
No drafts or hidden tenant data exposed; unpublished/nonexistent outlets both null/detail or empty item page
Do not expose internal merchant IDs, publication flags, memberships or identity/private fields
query_bounds: Strict canonical UUID parser for every ID/cursor; absent optional cursor accepted, malformed rejected BAD_USER_INPUT
limit default20 range1..50; lexicographic UUID keyset ORDER BY id ASC; fetch limit+1 and compute endCursor/hasNextPage
Allowlisted output fields; parameterized SQL; statement and connection deadlines; bounded SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE on DB failures
One SQL statement per query for consistent parent publication visibility; no caching stale publication status
constraints: No catalog seed/demo success in local runtime; synthetic DB fixtures only in tests
No onboarding/staff/publication mutations until authorization and policy packets
Preserve all prior dirty files and running apps
acceptance: Real migrations applied to PostgreSQL; defaults/checks/FK constraints reject invalid and cross-outlet records
Real GraphQL positive queries and hidden merchant/outlet/category/item negative cases
No price precision loss; pagination no duplicates and accurate page boundaries
Invalid IDs/cursors/limits fail bounded; no SQL errors/private data leak
DB outage fail closed, recovery works
